pol09_best_pick_composed_v1_tiebreak_dis.description: Tie-break audit: in the weeks where the production Best Pick pool ties at the top, the dispersion tie-break's nominee vs the alphabetical game_id fallback (nfl_ats.best_pick_nomination.select_nominee_v3) on the same pool, both settled on the ACTIVE model's pick side, top-1 hit rate; descriptive, tie weeks only
pol09_best_pick_composed_v1_tiebreak_dis.notes: Fourth reuse of the ~107-week opener population for the Best Pick family (ridge_alpha promotion look, odds-microstructure battery, 2026-08-18 ranker screen, 2026-08-19 v3 audit) -- compounding look-reuse discount. No rotation window assigned or spent: a scoring of an already-played rule. Population: 1,537 games, 107 weeks, seasons 2020-2025. Nominees settle on the ACTIVE model's pick (baseline_correct_open), not the candidate arm's; the 2026-08-19 v3 audit's 54.37% was the candidate-arm read. Bootstrap: seed 20260817, 20,000 draws, week-blocked, within-week correlation zero. v1 sweep refit reproduction max |residual diff| vs archive: 3.47 (probability_method gaussian_median). Nominees differ in 2 of 5 paired weeks; the outcome differs in 1.
pol09_best_pick_composed_v1_tiebreak_dis.plain_summary: When two games tie for the week's Best Pick, we now break the tie toward the game the sportsbooks agree on most instead of alphabetical order. That happened in only 5 weeks, and the two ways picked a different game in 2 of them; the new tie-break came out -20 points a week against the alphabetical choice there. One week's difference, far too few to call either way.
